simple.meaning: שָׁלָב (shâlâb) is a Hebrew word meaning “a spacer or raised interval , i.e. the stile in a frame or panel.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שָׁלָב (H7948) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 7:28, with occurrences in 1 Kings.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁלָב (H7948) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שָׁלָב (H7948) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שָׁלָב (shâlâb) / H7948 is traced through 1 Kings 7:28, 1 Kings 7:29 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The work of the bases was like this: they had panels; and there were panels between the ledges;

timeline.evidenceText: The work of the bases was like this: they had panels; and there were panels between the ledges;
and on the panels that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and cherubim; and on the ledges there was a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
